concerns.why: The `OR` array's second branch contains only `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduledDate` bound, unlike the first branch.

concerns.advisory: Reminders that exhaust their retries are hard-deleted with only a `console.log(...)` of the error, leaving no metric, alert, or persisted failure state, so a sustained Twilio/provider outage would silently drop customer-facing SMS reminders with no signal.
concerns.why: The catch block increments retryCount then only `console.log`s; the delete branch at the top of the handler removes those rows on the next cron run with no record of why.

concerns.advisory: retryCount is updated via a read-modify-write (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) rather than an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so overlapping or retried cron invocations processing the same reminder can lose increments and let a permanently failing reminder retry more times than intended.
concerns.why: Both new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls set `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` from the value read earlier in the handler.

concerns.advisory: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block is itself un-guarded and awaited, so a database error while recording the retry will propagate out of the catch and abort processing of all remaining reminders in the batch.
concerns.why: The `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` is the first statement in the `catch` and is not wrapped in its own try/catch.

concerns.advisory: The retry cap is an unnamed literal `gt: 1` in a delete query far from the two increment sites, meaning the effective policy (two attempts, cleanup deferred to the next cron tick) is undocumented and easy to break when either side is edited.
concerns.why: `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` appears in the `deleteMany` at the top of the handler with no constant, comment, or reference to the increment logic added below.

concerns.why: The diff adds three new behavioral branches in scheduleSMSReminders.ts and a schema column, with no test files touched.
